# Lie Algebra of $\mathrm{SL}_n$

**Claim.** The Lie algebra $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{SL}_n)$ equals $\mathfrak{sl}_n(k) = \{X \in M_n(k) : \operatorname{tr}(X) = 0\}$, with bracket $[X,Y]=XY-YX$.

---

## Setup

The special linear group is the affine algebraic group
$$\mathrm{SL}_n = \{A \in M_n(k) : \det(A) = 1\} \subseteq \mathrm{GL}_n.$$
It is the kernel of the determinant morphism of algebraic groups
$$\det : \mathrm{GL}_n \to \mathbb{G}_m, \qquad A \mapsto \det(A).$$

Recall that for a morphism of algebraic groups $f:G\to H$ with $f(e_G)=e_H$, the differential $df_{e_G}:\mathrm{Lie}(G)\to\mathrm{Lie}(H)$ is a morphism of Lie algebras, and when $f$ is a homomorphism with kernel $K$, there is an exact sequence of Lie algebras
$$0 \to \mathrm{Lie}(K) \to \mathrm{Lie}(G) \xrightarrow{df_e} \mathrm{Lie}(H).$$
In particular $\mathrm{Lie}(K) = \ker(df_e)$.

Applying this to $\det:\mathrm{GL}_n\to\mathbb{G}_m$ with $K=\mathrm{SL}_n$:
$$\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{SL}_n) = \ker\!\big(d(\det)_I : \mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{GL}_n) \to \mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_m)\big).$$

We know $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{GL}_n)=M_n(k)$ (tangent space at $I$ to the open subset $\det\neq 0$ of affine space $M_n$) and $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathbb{G}_m)=k$.

---

## Computing the differential of the determinant

Take $X\in M_n(k)$ and the curve $\gamma(t)=I+tX$ in $\mathrm{GL}_n$ with $\gamma(0)=I$, $\gamma'(0)=X$. Then
$$\det(I+tX) = 1 + t\,\operatorname{tr}(X) + O(t^2).$$
This is the standard first-order expansion of the determinant: the coefficient of $t$ is the sum of diagonal entries of $X$, i.e. the trace. (Equivalently, the derivative of $\det$ at $I$ in direction $X$ is the directional derivative $\sum_i \partial\det/\partial a_{ii}\cdot X_{ii}$, and each $\partial\det/\partial a_{ii}|_I = 1$.)

Hence
$$d(\det)_I(X) = \operatorname{tr}(X).$$

---

## Conclusion

Therefore
$$\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{SL}_n) = \ker(d(\det)_I) = \{X\in M_n(k) : \operatorname{tr}(X)=0\} = \mathfrak{sl}_n(k).$$

The Lie bracket is inherited from $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{GL}_n)=\mathfrak{gl}_n(k)$, where it is the commutator $[X,Y]=XY-YX$. The subspace $\mathfrak{sl}_n(k)$ is closed under this bracket because
$$\operatorname{tr}([X,Y])=\operatorname{tr}(XY)-\operatorname{tr}(YX)=0,$$
using $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$. So $\mathfrak{sl}_n(k)$ is a Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak{gl}_n(k)$.

**Dimension check.** $\dim\mathrm{SL}_n = n^2-1$ (one equation $\det=1$ cut out of $\mathrm{GL}_n$), and $\dim\mathfrak{sl}_n = n^2-1$ (one linear condition $\operatorname{tr}=0$ on $M_n$). The dimensions agree, consistent with $\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{SL}_n)=\mathfrak{sl}_n(k)$.

---

$$\boxed{\mathrm{Lie}(\mathrm{SL}_n) = \mathfrak{sl}_n(k) = \{X\in M_n(k) : \operatorname{tr}(X)=0\}, \quad [X,Y]=XY-YX.}$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
